A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLsI work and support comparison of the text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The qualitative appendices match after accounting for renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original VLsI benchmark results, component ablations, layer-matching analyses, and qualitative outputs in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds beam-decoding and uniform-matching results plus layerwise verbalization-loss trajectories.

M1.justification: The verbalizers, adaptive layer matching, interaction loss, and final supervised training procedure are retained. Renaming the reinforcement step to supervised finetuning (SFT) clarifies terminology without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The visual-instruction training mixture and benchmark coverage remain unchanged. The added decoding, matching, and loss analyses introduce no new datasets, domains, or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 4(e) adds Uniform Index to the existing layer-matching comparators. Comparator membership in Tables 1–3 is unchanged; the newly cited distillation methods are discussed without being added to those evaluations.

E3.justification: Table 4(b) adds beam decoding for the 2B and 7B models without SFT; Appendix D specifies N=5. The existing benchmark protocols and stated training settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 extends the existing ablations with uniform layer matching and beam decoding without SFT. New Appendix B reports losses for seven target layers at six training-progress checkpoints, adding a limited analysis of verbalization training.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its experiments. The added loss trajectories do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results. V2 adds beam/no-SFT results, including 7B MM-Vet 70.9 and MMMU 63.5, Uniform Index results of 66.5 and 55.3 on those benchmarks, and Appendix B loss trajectories. These are additional results under newly reported conditions.

T1.justification: The layer-order constraints and interaction-loss formulation are unchanged, with no added theoretical assumptions, proofs, or derivations. The new Uniform Index pseudocode documents an experimental comparator.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the explicit 19.7% Qwen2-VL and 34.5% LLaVA-OV improvement claims and recasts the contribution list to emphasize dynamic layer matching. The central distillation claim and abstract’s 11.0%/17.4% comparisons with GPT-4V remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly interprets the beam-decoding results as suggesting that interaction expands the language-head probability space and SFT aligns it with instruction following. The existing same-tokenizer and token-index-order limitation is retained.

D1.justification: V2 specifies beam width N=5 and supplies Uniform Index pseudocode using floor(t_l/t_s) layer spacing. Existing hardware, optimizer, LoRA settings, dataset preparation information, and project-page access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds TED, Align-KD, MoVE-KD, DistiLLM, MiniLLM, and LLAVADI. It expands comparisons concerning language heads, unequal layer counts, and KL-divergence direction, while retaining the earlier references and overall research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 revises the contribution summary, expands the distillation-related discussion, renames reinforcement to SFT, and updates affiliation information. Inserting Appendix B changes subsequent appendix labels; most existing prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the Appendix B loss table, expands and resizes Tables 4(b) and 4(e), and explains the training-status icons in Figure 2’s caption. Appendix material shifts, while existing plots and qualitative example content are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves clarity through the SFT terminology and closer comparisons with prior distillation work. The added matching and decoding controls, together with loss trajectories, provide useful support for existing design choices. These gains are limited: the core method and headline benchmark results remain unchanged, and the new mechanism explanation is still tentative.
